items.title: Wales lose to Denmark, Portugal win without Ronaldo, Haaland limps off: Nations League – as it happened
items.summary: A howler from Ward cost Wales against Denmark while a Portugal side without Ronaldo got the job done against Norway, who saw Haaland limp off.Five minutes before it all kicks off. Here are some quick stats and facts:Greece’s 1-0 win in the reverse fixture was their first victory over Germany in 11 meetings. Dimitris Kourbelis scored the only goal.Greece lead the group on seven points from three games; Germany are third on four.Germany arrive after a 2-0 win over Serbia, their first victory under Jürgen Klopp.The Netherlands won 2-1 in Belgrade last month, with Mexx Meerdink scoring twice, including the winner.Meerdink’s brace came on his first international start, in only his second senior appearance for the Netherlands.Serbia have lost all three group games so far, while the Netherlands are unbeaten after a win and two draws.Portugal have won all three group games and lead Group A4 on nine points.The sides have already met once in this Nations League: Portugal won 2-1 in Oslo, with João Félix and Gonçalo Ramos scoring.Norway’s Erling Haaland has scored three goals in the group so far.Denmark beat Wales 2-0 in Copenhagen last month, with Ben Davies turning in Mikkel Damsgaard’s cross before Gustav Isaksen scored.Wales bounced back with a 2-1 win over Norway on Thursday, their first victory of the group campaign.Denmark have won eight of the teams’ 12 meetings, with Wales winning four; they have never drawn.Ireland won the first meeting 3-0 last week, scoring all three goals in the first 25 minutes.Troy Parrott has scored three times across Ireland’s last two games: once against Israel, then twice against Austria.The match is being played behind closed doors at a neutral venue in Bačka Topola, Serbia, after being moved from Dublin. items.title: Denmark sink Wales as Rasmus Højlund makes Danny Ward pay for blunder
items.summary: Wales crave momentum but, a few days after surely the sweetest high of Craig Bellamy’s two-year reign, a sapping international window ended on a bum note. At least until Bellamy was informed Portugal’s comeback victory over Norway means Wales will spend the next six weeks in third, and not bottom of Nations League A4 owing to their superior head-to-record. “That’s actually quite nice,” the Wales head coach said, slowly digesting the silver lining about half an hour after the final whistle. “That’s brightened up a real rubbish moment.”Bellamy suggested last Thursday’s victory over Norway blew the group wide open with a hand grenade but Danny Ward detonated one to give Denmark a second-half penalty and Rasmus Højlund’s flawless spot-kick ultimately proved the difference. The galling thing for Ward was that until his moment of madness, he had kept his country in the game, his best stop a sublime right-hand save to deny Gustav Isaksen. A first clean sheet since beating Liechtenstein last November also went out of the window for Wales. The life of a goalkeeper, eh? Continue reading...

items.title: Jesse Marsch: ‘We Americans have been inundated with propaganda since we were young’
items.summary: As he prepares to face his home nation, the Canada manager reflects on his adopted country’s soccer, its prime minister, and its place in the worldPeak leaf hasn’t yet arrived in Montreal but the bursts of gold and butterscotch up on the hill that gave this place its name still mushroom out by the hour.Sitting in a glass-panelled hotel mezzanine at the foot of Mount Royal, Canada men’s coach Jesse Marsch has his mind on another harvest. When this extended autumnal international window ends, he will decamp to Italy, where the olive crops at his Tuscan villa are ready for reaping. Continue reading...

items.title: Republicans say they hate communists. So why do they like Donald Trump?
items.summary: Trump supporters may be surprised to learn the state takeover of means of production is not driven by the leftAmericans will never accept the Democratic party’s slide to the left, or so desperate Republicans are hoping.With the midterm elections fast upon us, Zohran Mamdani’s promise of a few city-run bodegas in New York City will scare the bejeezus out of middle America. Disgust over the democratic socialists’ unicorn-and-puppy promises of a world without capitalism will keep the Republicans in power. Continue reading...

items.title: ‘We are in a kind of war’: row over viral Amsterdam chip shop lands in court
items.summary: Neighbours say crowds drawn by TikTok to Fabel Friet are clogging the picturesque canal street and attracting litter, gulls and ratsPeople living in one of Amsterdam’s most exclusive neighbourhoods have taken the city to court for licensing a chip shop that has gone viral on TikTok.On busy days, the queue for Fabel Friet on Runstraat stretches across a bridge on the Keizersgracht – one of Amsterdam’s most famous canals – a court was told last week. The narrow street itself is crowded by tourists waiting for their orders seven days a week. And loitering with intent – on parked cars, on the street itself, and on steps and porches – gulls wait to swoop. Continue reading...
